evidence.note: Opening plan: understand ISA first, notes baseline 147,734 and target <1250, reasons about per-round cycle floor — establishes phases but no explicit intermediate gate ladder.
Commits to a single ambitious 'mathematical path to <1250' design (MUX tree + multiply_add) rather than staging correct-rewrite → vectorized → packed with checkpoints; a big-bang push.
git checkout /app/kernel.py to recover after clobbering it — shows no preserved known-good intermediate version was maintained as a fallback rung.

A real ordered progression of intermediate cycle observations (3198→2553→2293→1248/block) driven by lane-count (L) tuning, with loose targets '<1500'/'<2000' — phase work in rough order but organic, not pre-planned gates.
First run_tests.sh runs only near the very end; final ~2357 cycles. Correctness-first then parallelize sequencing is present but never crystallized into a gated milestone ladder.

reasoning: The agent identified a few genuine phases (understand → design → get correct → increase parallelism to cut cycles) and worked them roughly in order, tracking intermediate cycle counts as it tuned lanes — matching the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because there was no explicit milestone ladder with pre-set quantitative gates and, decisively, no preserved known-good version at each rung (it pursued one large design, debugged it in scratch files, and needed a git checkout to recover). It exceeds level 3 because the phasing and intermediate cycle checkpoints were real rather than a single undifferentiated 'make it faster' push.
